external_authority.boundary: The cited GRS theorems are stated for one real scalar. This package records the finite-eight-component extension by exposing the exact component-blind spectral argument and separately discharging Q3 coercivity, line-cutoff FKN and open-rectangle coordinate exchange, while isolating the massive periodic boundary comparison as the open uniform surface-pairing gate. No world-first claim is made.

setup.parameters: m0>0, g>0, lambda>=0, K_pl any fixed real symmetric 8 by 8 matrix, and scalar density e_pl
setup.centered_density: u(x)=:P_pl(Phi(x)):_(C_pl) with the field-independent scalar removed, where P_pl(q)=q^T K_pl q/2+W4(q)
setup.coercivity: W4(q)>=g|q|^4/32; this full radial coercivity, not mere pointwise boundedness, is the load-bearing multivariate normalizability input
setup.sharp_cutoff: H_l^sharp=H0+int_(-l/2)^(l/2)u(x)dx on Fock space over L2(R;C8), E_l^sharp=inf spec H_l^sharp, Z(t,l)=<Omega0,exp(-tH_l^sharp)Omega0>
setup.periodic_centering: Hhat_s=H_s-T_s I for the EXP-000775 circle Hamiltonian, so E0(Hhat_s)=E_s-T_s

finite_component_GRS_extension.normalizability_firewall: The mixed-polynomial counterexample P(x1,x2)=x1^2 x2^2 is nonnegative but not radially coercive and does not satisfy the Q3 estimate. EXP-000772's Boue-Dupuis/Nelson estimate and the g>0 bound supply the missing uniform integrability for Q3.
finite_component_GRS_extension.line_Hamiltonian: The finite Q3 monomial list and product-Gaussian hypercontractive estimates construct every H_l^sharp as a closed lower-bounded spatially cutoff P(Phi)2 Hamiltonian with a positive ground and nonzero overlap with Omega0. The support-uniform Glimm-Jaffe/Simon localizability bound is a separate finite-component constructive input and is linear in l; a fixed-time L1-to-L2 Nelson bound gives the exponential ground-overlap estimate used for aspect-ratio-uniform open rectangles.
finite_component_GRS_extension.open_rectangle_FKN: Z(t,l) equals the plane Gaussian expectation of exp[-int_(R_txl)u] and the isotropic plane covariance plus one plane-Wick convention gives Z(t,l)=Z(l,t).
finite_component_GRS_extension.spectral_Holder: For 0<a<1 and positive A, <psi,A^a psi><=<psi,A psi>^a. Taking A=exp(-lH_t^sharp), using Nelson symmetry, and then the ground spectral limit gives Z(t,al)<=Z(t,l)^a and alpha(al)<=alpha(l), where alpha(l)=-E_l^sharp/l.
finite_component_GRS_extension.bounded_limit: The linear Nelson lower bound makes alpha bounded above, so alpha_infinity=lim_(l->infinity)alpha(l) exists and is finite.
finite_component_GRS_extension.strictness: Plane Wick centering gives q_l[Omega0]=0, while the pure four-particle projection has strictly positive norm; hence Omega0 is not a ground vector, E_l^sharp<0, alpha(l)>0, and alpha_infinity>0.
finite_component_GRS_extension.boundary_reduction: At finite cutoff Gaussian interpolation gives an exact derivative formula for the periodic-versus-plane log partition. Closing an O(boundary) estimate requires a normalized interacting Wick-derivative insertion bound uniform in ultraviolet cutoff, rectangle size and interpolation parameter. EXP-000772 fixed-volume uniform integrability does not supply this theorem; the periodic bridge remains open.

strict_witness.curvature_cross_check: sigma^2=int_R2 Cov_0(u(x),u(0))dx >= [21 zeta(3)/(16 pi^3 m0^2)](g+3lambda)^2>0, using int_R2 C_m(x)^4 dx=7 zeta(3)/(64 pi^3 m0^2)
strict_witness.curvature_boundary: The curvature identity is an independent sign and factor audit. Strict thermodynamic positivity is proved by the GRS monotonicity route, not by assuming a volume-uniform Taylor remainder.

zero_temperature_reduction.periodic_energy_conditional: if the uniform surface-pairing lemma proves (E_s^(per,u)-E_s^sharp)/s->0, then the exact Wick ledger E0(Hhat_s)=E_s^(per,u)-s c_s with c_s->0 gives lim_(s->infinity)E0(Hhat_s)/s=-alpha_infinity<0
zero_temperature_reduction.joint_van_Hove_conditional: under rectangle-uniform boundary comparison, the centered relative pressure/specific-KL scalar has the same alpha_infinity joint and iterated limits
zero_temperature_reduction.scalar_ledger: T_beta/beta=e_(*,beta)->e_pl is closed; the further conclusion E_beta/beta->e_pl-alpha_infinity remains conditional on the periodic-sharp bridge. Adding c shifts both finite-beta terms and leaves every centered gap invariant.
zero_temperature_reduction.finite_beta_witness_nogo: the EXP-000775 four-zero-mode amplitude is O(beta^-1); pointwise E_beta<T_beta alone is compatible with a zero density limit and cannot replace the sharp-cutoff GRS argument
zero_temperature_reduction.state_boundary: Only scalar pressures, energies and specific-KL densities are interchanged. States, ground vectors, order parameters, spectral gaps and correlation functions are not interchanged.

physical_and_phase_boundary.physical_empty_space: the Gaussian reference is not independently derived as cosmic empty space or the no-condensate state; no physical below-empty-space claim follows

prior_art_boundary: GRS prove the scalar sharp-cutoff monotonicity and vacuum-energy limit, and later scalar work proves boundary independence. Their spectral-Holder core is component-blind, but no located primary source states this eight-component nonradial Q3 theorem verbatim. Nagoji shows why mere multivariate stability is insufficient; the Q3 g>0 radial coercivity and EXP-000772 estimates are essential. No located source proves the full TECT Pre-A chain.
no_overclaim: This theorem proves a strict infinite-line sharp-cutoff centered vacuum-energy density below one named massive Gaussian reference for a newly declared inserted Q3 P(Phi)2 family. It does not yet prove the periodic zero-temperature or joint scalar van-Hove limit because the normalized Wick-derivative surface-pairing estimate remains open. It does not identify the Gaussian with physical empty space, fix an absolute gravitational vacuum energy, select a phase, prove a cosmological phase transition, interchange states or gaps, construct the original fixed-raw CL8 or three-dimensional parent, derive light, close C0 or N1-N5, advance C6, complete CP1 or Sector A, or prove Pre-A.
